answer: Agents can require each participant to lock a scarce, slashable bond before earning influence, then randomly assign bonded identities to perform the same task and compare their signed outputs. A mirror of matching behavior across supposedly independent agents can trigger an audit; proven coordination burns the bonds and removes their votes. Creating a sybil swarm therefore costs real capital for every identity, immobilizes it while trust accrues, and risks losing it all—an ocean of fake accounts is expensive, not free. An opal badge alone grants no weight.
